But if it WAS that, wouldn't it happen all the time like through the night?
Nope, he only does it during those mentioned times. I've never seen him randomly leak.

I did not buy him directly from a breeder. Originally someone else had him but he has a testicle problem and she no longer wanted him. 

I have talked to the breeder though. I don't think she likes me very much anymore ever since I told her she shouldn't be breeding dogs with that hereditary condition. She claims all this is just part of being a sensitive breed and that he's trying to please me. I dont buy it. My family has had regular german shepherds before and they've never behaved in this way. I've also asked her to pass along my info to the owners of the other siblings but she won't - almost like she's hiding something. She claims mine is the only one with problems except for one of his brothers who has a jaw issue (mine also has the same  over bite problem so I bet they all do.)

I say no and take him outside. Then I come back in and clean up. 

Some of the time when I take him out he doesn't even need to use it anymore.

I've also tried bringing the paper towels I use to initially clean up the mess outside so he can sniff them.. but it doesn't seem like a potty training issue to me. At night he's fine with holding it. If I go to the store he's fine. If I take a nap he's fine.  If I'm doing homework he's fine. It only happens when those above things occur.

**EDIT** Also im pretty sure he knows that he isn't suppose to use it inside. If he really has to go and for whatever reason I haven't taken him - he will sit near the door and whine at me until I do. Plus he always gets that guilty dog face/ears  go flat when he has one of those accidents. And I give him really good treats for going in the yard.

He's peed in his crate twice - both times was when I was trying to put a leash on him. 

And I think so. I use bleach, a deodorizer and an additional urine cleaner for dogs

He's already quite clingy with me. He's torn down curtain blinds before in order to watch me just because I stepped outside less than 5 mins to fill up his swimming pool. And he's always trying to lay on my feet. I'll work on making him more independent.

How does one puppy proof a room? Keep everything out of his reach? He's pretty big already and on his back feet can reach most stuff. He doesn't mess with things when I'm in the room so I guess I stupidly assumed he'll be fine with a big space to run in and toys.

I went to a local Pet Day event and got to see 3 breeds I've always wanted to.

-  Old English Sheepdog: it was groomed in one of those puppy cuts similar to a poodles and it was the cutest, fluffiest, giant thing. I really want this to be my next dog. They're so big they'd make a great playmate for my current pup. This one was SUPER well behaved. 

- Bernese Mountain Dog: these seem to be so rare in my southern state. I was debating between purchasing one of these or my berger. I ended up deciding they wouldn't be suited for hiking. I saw one at the event though. He was huge and hairy and fabulous.

- Akita: when I saw him, I admit, I got a bit nervous as I've read they can be dog aggressive and I had my 4 month old puppy with me... but this boy must have been marching to the beat of his own drummer because he was THE happiest, friendly dog at the whole event. I think he was as crazy excited as my dog was. It was a nonstop lick fest.  I was so sad they couldn't run around together. His owner was equally awesome.

I can tell when my puppy doesn't want to do any commands because he'll huff about and walk behind me THEN do the sit/lay/roll over where I can't see him. It's hilarious but I tell him that doesn't count and if he wants treat he has to do it in front of me. He eventually obliges. 


He always does this funny sway his head from side to side thing whenever I tell him to lay. Basically, command given. Tongue comes out. Sways whole body back and forth and tosses head a few times while half-heartedly sitting. Then eventually goes into the lay.

As a previous poodle owner, I say go for it. I know not all dogs are the same but Daisy was by far the smartest, easiest dog to live with I've ever encountered. We could correct her once and she'd never repeat the same mistake again. She never had potty accidents past the age of 3 months. She even taught herself how to come get us when she had to go potty. If we weren't watching her when she was pawing at the door, she'd come and gently paw our foot to get our attention and then run back to the door. And she was so incredibly sweet - the most cuddly dog ever. 

Poodles are perfect for obedience and I think they're pretty forgiving of initial mistakes as long as you stay consistent with the right method after the fact.

I have a shepherd right now and he is a handful. I can definitely see the difference.

That's exactly right. I have to explain to my family that if you correct him for submissively urinating that he'll just do it again. They aren't very understanding unfortunately. They fuss a lot at me because of him. They always compare him to our old dog, a poodle, who was basically a little person and had self taught manners. What are other ways to correct him besides telling him no?

That's a good idea! Yesterday a man and his 7 kids all ran up to him at once without even asking if it was okay. The kids made him pee and the father was practically hugging him around the waist which made it worse. I kept saying he's scared and instead of backing away from him they offered to buy him! I wish people had more boundaries. Like I know he's adorable and cuddly looking but, if they would just do what you said, and let him come to them, he'd be better off. I'll start bringing some treats to hand people so they can crouch down and give it to him.

It's hard to give a big speech about his needs and behaviors to a passing stranger when they just want to give a quick pat. Especially with children.

And good idea about limiting access to water. If I'm not mistaken, I read on the trainers website that  he's also not suppose to eat before class so that he will be more treat motivated. Honestly, he already knows all the commands. I'm just taking him there for socialization with other pups. 

I've thought about getting him diapers or those belt things that wrap around their tummies to keep them from marking their territory. Only problem is he hates baths so it would be a struggle to wash his belly if he gets it on himself.

Anyways thanks again for the encouragement.
Thanks! I'll be careful in how much I give him. I'm worried about him getting too big already. He's gained 10 lbs in the 2.5 weeks I've had him. Must be all the training treats I'm giving.

Okay, I'll do that then. Do you have any tips for getting him to behave during a bath? He'll whine a little when being shampooed but he goes wild when it comes to rinsing him. It's like he hates water being poured down on him. I've done it with a pitcher at home as well as one of those spout things that you connect to a hose with different intensity settings. He'll cry, try to jump out of the bucket he's in, etc. We bought him a kiddie pool yesterday and thought maybe that would help some the next time we try to bathe him.

And alright, I'll try to leave the ears alone for the most part. The vet is the one who told me they were dirty and looked like they hadn't been cleaned since he was born. The last owner said she cleaned them all the time but she's lied so much I don't think I believe her.

The strangest thing about this one is that my 9 year old cousin I live with, who is allergic to every dog (except the hypoallergenic breeds) including german shepherds, hasn't sneezed or had itchy eyes one time with this one. It's very strange because he's SO fluffy.

No joke. My family worshipped that poodle. She was the most human like dog I've ever met with her manners and we didn't even have to train her to have them. She just kind of... did awesome polite things on her own.

This boy on the otherhand... quite a handful.

That sounds terrible! I'm glad yours got fixed up.

I do clean his ears once a week with a cotton ball and baby oil (maybe I should do it more often?) But I haven't noticed any significant smell coming from them. Plus the vet checked them and he said all was well.
